newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:
* Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Saturday the government will not raise domestic fuel oil prices, at least until the end of 1997.

* On Friday, the Dow was again in new high ground, gaining 67.73 points to close at 6,833.10 and beating Thursday's record close of 6,765.37. The leap in stock prices has been generated by an explosion in corporate profits, which have jumped nearly 140 percent since 1991.
* The Jakarta Composite Index rose 5.27 points, or 0.80 percent, to close at 663.97 points on Friday due to active buying in Telkom and other big-capitalised stocks.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,370.25/70.75 in early trading against the opening of 2,370.25/71.25.
* Cocoa butter processor PT Cahaya Kalbar as it plans to invest around 10 billion rupiah on expansion in 1997.
* Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma on news that it plans to acquire the assets of two Australian firms worth around $14.75 million.
* Light metal manufacturer Alumindo as it plans to lower its shareholding in PT Maspion Stainless Steel Industry to 70 percent from 87.5 percent.
* Toll road builder and operator Citra Marga on reports it plans to issue a 250 billion rupiah bond to finance its toll road project in East Java.
* Conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers on market talk it planned to sell its 49 percent stake in PT Indocopper Investama, which owns a 9.36 percent stake in gold miner PT Freeport Indonesia.
* Indosat following the signing of a $1.3 billion submarine cable deal in Singapore by a consortium of telecommunications firm of which Indosat is a member.
* Distribution firm Enseval on market talk of a possible link-up with a foreign partner.
* Bank BNI on news it plans to issue $145 million Yankee bonds through its New York office
